00010b20.answer: SETTLED, no hoist. The built object recomputes the product in the loop head exactly as 00010b20 does. Disassembled the code bytes of the existing workspace/code_emit/out/objs/MOVEGRID.OBJ (LEDATA payload at file offset 0x0192; the object holds only fdps_map_grid_reset): the loop head at payload +0x3e (file offset 0x1d0) is 8b 45 f8 / 0f af 45 f4 / 3b 45 f0 / 7f 07 / eb 18 = MOV EAX,[EBP-0x8] / IMUL EAX,[EBP-0xc] / CMP EAX,[EBP-0x10] / JG body / JMP epilogue -- five instructions, the same SHAPE as 00010b5e-00010b6a with the IMUL inside the head and re-executed every pass. Not the same operands: the original reads the product out of [EBP-0x10] and compares against [EBP-0x8], the rebuild the other way round, because the two frame slots are assigned in the other order (see residual). That is which slot holds what, not whether the multiply is in the loop, which is the only thing this concern asked. The reason is the flag set itself: rebuild_info/build_flags.md fixes it at 'wcc386 -bt=dos4g -mf -4s -fpi -s -ot -od', and -od turns the optimiser off (the same flag that keeps every local written back to the stack, which this object also shows -- both dimension slots and the index are re-read from the frame in the head). No loop-invariant motion runs, so there is nothing to hoist the product out. The emitted C needed no change and gets none: it already spells the recomputation, and the built code proves the spelling survives the toolchain. Contract D closes for this loop.
